summary: 新月形沙丘可以一边移动一边维持形状，有些甚至会“唱歌”。研究者从风与沙粒的运动入手，并用取样实验追查声响的来源。

paragraphs.brief: 对工业设施和通信的潜在威胁。
sentences: Armies of giant sand dunes are advancing across the world’s deserts, engulfing anything that crosses their path.
巨大的沙丘军队正在穿越世界沙漠，吞没着穿越其道路的一切。
They are tens of metres tall and hundreds of metres long.
它们有数十米高，数百米长。
Fortunately, they aren’t going very fast.
幸运的是，他们走的不快。

Even the smallest, speediest dunes only travel about 100 metres over the course of a year, while the bigger ones, which weigh something in the order of 10,000 tonnes, barely move one metre in that time.
即使是最小的、最快速的沙丘一年中只行走100米左右而较大的沙丘重量大约在10000吨左右
However, their insidious creep can have serious consequences if there is an oil installation or a railway line in their path.
然而，如果在他们的道路上有一个石油装置或铁路线，他们阴险的爬行可能会造成严重的后果。
About 47% of the world’s land mass, including Antarctica, most of Australia and large areas of Africa, is classified as arid or semi-arid desert.
世界上大约47%的陆地，包括南极洲、澳大利亚大部分和非洲大片地区，被划为干旱或半干旱沙漠。
Only around 20% of that is sand-covered, however, and over half of that is classified as ‘linear’ sand dunes.
但其中只有大约20%是被沙覆盖的，超过一半被归类为 " 线性 " 沙丘。
These form in a long curving wave, as a result of wind blowing strongly from several quarters, flipping them from side to side.
这些形态是长长的弯曲波，由几处强烈的风吹来，将它们从侧向侧翻转。
Although linear dunes are static, sand blowing off them can cause problems for desert villages, burying crops and buildings.
虽然线性沙丘是静态的，但沙子吹散沙丘可能会给沙漠村庄造成问题，埋藏作物和建筑物。

paragraphs.brief: 需要特定条件同时具备。
sentences: Moving dunes make up just a small percentage of the rest, but they are of the most interest to scientists.
移动沙丘只是其他沙丘的一小部分，但它们是科学家们最感兴趣的。
They are known as ‘barchans’: heavy, crescent-shaped sand piles with a ridged crest and two elongated arms, one curving away to either side.
他们被称为 " 巴特恩人 " :堆积着一头被剥掉的圆顶和两只长臂，一个弯曲到两边。

‘Barchan dunes only tend to form where you have one-directional winds on the edge of sandy deserts near coastal areas,’ says Giles Wiggs, a geomorphologist at Oxford University, who has been studying the formation and movement of sand dunes for more than a decade.
牛津大学地质学家吉尔斯·维格斯 (Giles Wiggs) 说："巴尔坎沙丘只会在沿海地区附近沙漠边缘出现单向风的形成。
But even with strong winds, how can entire barchans move while retaining their form?
但是即使风力强劲整个酒吧怎么能在保持其形态的同时移动呢？
That question was first answered in the mid-20th century by British explorer Ralph Alger Bagnold, and his answer hinges on the fact that dunes aren’t solid, but granular.
20世纪中叶，英国探险家Ralph Alger Bagnold首次回答了这个问题，他的回答取决于沙丘不是固体而是颗粒这一事实。
Bagnold figured out how barchan dunes are able to move grain by grain.
巴格诺德想通了巴钱沙丘如何用谷物移动谷物
Imagine a single grain of sand being blown up the back of a dune by the wind and deposited on the top.
想象一下一粒沙子被风吹到沙丘的后背并沉到顶部
More grains follow the same pattern, until the accumulated weight of piled-up sand finally pushes the top down the dune face.
更多的谷物遵循同样的模式，直到堆积沙堆积起来的重量最终推向沙丘的顶部。
The grain tumbles, then stops on the face until subsequent mini-avalanches bury it.
谷物倒塌，然后停止在脸上直到后来的迷你瓦兰切埋了它。
Eventually, it reappears at the back of the dune, ready to repeat the process.
最终，它重新出现在沙丘的后面，准备重复这一进程。
As this happens to every grain of sand in the dune, the whole thing creeps in the direction of the prevailing wind.
当沙丘上的每一粒沙子都这样的时候整件事就朝风向爬去
The relationship between the wind and barchan dunes is complex.
风和巴尚沙丘之间的关系是复杂的。
As a dune grows, it modifies the speed and course of the wind, which in turn alters how that dune and its neighbours evolve.
随着沙丘的增长，它改变了风的速度和航向，反过来又改变了沙丘及其邻国的演变方式。
‘Interestingly, the dune can regulate its own shape, and maintain it as it moves,’ says Dr Stéphane Douady, a physicist at École Normale Supérieure (ENS) in France.
Stéphane Douady博士，法国高等高等学院的物理学家：“有趣的是，沙丘可以调节自己的形状，并随着它移动而保持它。”
‘Even when two dunes collide, they quickly take on their distinctive shapes again.
即使在两个沙丘相撞时，它们也迅速恢复其独特的形状。
It’s like a living organism.’
这就像一个活生物体。

paragraphs.brief: 古老迷信得到科学解释。
sentences: Douady and his colleagues have also been studying an even odder phenomenon than moving dunes: some barchans actually sing.
杜瓦迪和他的同事也在研究一种比移动沙丘更奇特的现象：一些酒吧实际上在唱歌。
Local legends attributed the sounds to dangerous spirits which were trying to trap unwary travellers.
当地传奇把声音归咎于试图困住不小心旅行者的危险的灵魂
Douady is more pragmatic.
杜瓦迪更实用
‘It’s a strong booming noise with a low frequency,’ he explains, making a noise like a foghorn to demonstrate.
他解释，制造噪音像雾号来示范：“低频率的强烈噪音。”
‘It can last for a long time – up to several minutes.
它可以持续很长时间，最多几分钟。
It’s a very loud sound and you don’t understand where it’s coming from when you first hear it.’
这是一个非常响亮的声音你不明白它从哪儿来当你第一次听到它。"
There are about 50 dunes distributed across 35 deserts round the world that are known to sing.
全世界有大约50个沙丘分布在35个沙漠中众所周知，它们会唱歌
Douady says the sound is caused by the way sand avalanches down the faces of particular dunes.
杜瓦迪说声音是沙雪压倒某个沙丘的表情造成的
Rather than tumbling randomly, the sand grains flow in synchrony and set each other vibrating like the membrane on a gigantic loudspeaker.
沙粒不是随意翻滚，而是同步流动，相互振动，就像膜一样，放在一个巨大的扬声器上。
The synchronisation causes the air to move in and out between the grains, creating a powerful sound wave.
同步导致空气在谷物之间流动，形成强大的声波。

paragraphs.brief: 在实验室重现这一过程。
sentences: What really surprised the scientists, however, was that they were able to take samples of the singing sand back to France and replicate the sound at ENS, proving that it’s the sand, not the dune shape, that causes the sound.
科学家们真正惊讶的是，他们能够把歌声沙子的样本带回法国，复制美国国家感应署的声音，证明是沙子而不是沙丘的形状造成声音。
Their studies show the grains are a uniform shape, well-rounded from years of striking each other, and that the variations in size affect the tone.
他们的研究显示，谷物的形状是统一的，与多年的碰撞相隔很远，大小的变化影响着音调。

Crucially, the grains are coated with a special veneer, which Douady calls ‘desert glaze’, made from a precise combination of minerals from surrounding rocks including iron, aluminium, manganese, silicon and calcium.
关键是，谷物涂上一种特殊的葡萄，杜瓦迪称之为“沙漠玻璃”，由周围岩石的精密混合矿物制成，包括铁、铝、锰、硅和钙。
The team found that after a month or so, the veneer wore off and the grains lost their ‘voice’.
调查组发现，大约一个月后，葡萄酒脱落，谷物失去“声音”。
‘We managed to reproduce the desert glaze and then the grains started to sing again,’ says Douady.
杜迪说：“我们复制了沙漠的玻璃然后谷物又开始唱歌了。”
‘We tried putting the coating onto different grains, but they weren’t round enough and it didn’t work.
我们试图把涂料放在不同的谷物上，但他们不够圆，它没有起作用。
But some American colleagues made some artificial grains and managed to make them sing, after covering them in desert glaze.’
但一些美国同事在沙漠中涂上蜡烛后，做了一些人工谷物，并设法让他们唱歌。
Douady has now made recordings of dunesong from all over the world which are to be made into a CD.
杜瓦迪现在录制了来自世界各地的沙尼翁，这些沙尼翁将被制成裁谈会。

items.zh: 为 A 段选择最能概括全段的标题。
items.answer: iv · A potential threat to industry and communications
items.solution: 对工业设施和交通线路的潜在威胁
items.cue: 巨大的沙丘军队正在穿越世界沙漠，吞没着穿越其道路的一切。
items.why: 沙丘移动虽慢，持续逼近仍可能危及道路、线路或其他基础设施。

items.zh: 为 B 段选择最能概括全段的标题。
items.answer: viii · The commonest type of dune
items.cue: 但其中只有大约20%是被沙覆盖的，超过一半被归类为 " 线性 " 沙丘。
items.why: 先从全球沙地面积讲起，再指出常见的是延伸成长条波形的线形沙丘。

items.zh: 为 C 段选择最能概括全段的标题。
items.answer: vi · Needing a specific combination of conditions
items.solution: 需要特定条件同时具备
items.cue: 移动沙丘只是其他沙丘的一小部分，但它们是科学家们最感兴趣的。
items.why: 新月形沙丘只会在风向和供沙等条件适宜的地点形成。

items.zh: 为 D 段选择最能概括全段的标题。
items.cue: 想象一下一粒沙子被风吹到沙丘的后背并沉到顶部
items.why: 跟随一粒沙走完上坡、滑落、被覆盖、再露出的全过程，便能解释沙丘整体前移。

items.zh: 为 E 段选择最能概括全段的标题。
items.answer: v · Dunes coming together and re-forming
items.cue: 风和巴尚沙丘之间的关系是复杂的。
items.why: 风与沙丘形状互相影响，两个沙丘相遇后还能很快重新形成自身的形态。

items.zh: 为 F 段选择最能概括全段的标题。
items.solution: 古老迷信得到科学解释
items.cue: 同步导致空气在谷物之间流动，形成强大的声波。
items.why: 传说把巨响归于危险精灵，研究者以沙粒同步滑动带动空气振动解释它。

items.zh: 为 G 段选择最能概括全段的标题。
items.answer: ii · Recreating the process in a laboratory
items.solution: 在实验室重现这一过程
items.cue: 但一些美国同事在沙漠中涂上蜡烛后，做了一些人工谷物，并设法让他们唱歌。
items.why: 研究者复制沙粒表层，尝试使沙粒重新发声，并比较实验室制造的颗粒。

options: 开头特意指出即使最快的沙丘也移动缓慢，威胁来自逐步逼近。
Recreating the process in a laboratory
在实验室重现这一过程
研究者复制沙粒表层，尝试使沙粒重新发声，并比较实验室制造的颗粒。
Strange music created by human movement
人类动作产生的奇异音乐
沙丘的轰鸣归因于沙粒同步运动；人们听见声音不等于由人制造声音。
A potential threat to industry and communications
对工业设施和交通线路的潜在威胁
沙丘移动虽慢，持续逼近仍可能危及道路、线路或其他基础设施。
风与沙丘形状互相影响，两个沙丘相遇后还能很快重新形成自身的形态。
Needing a specific combination of conditions
需要特定条件同时具备
新月形沙丘只会在风向和供沙等条件适宜的地点形成。
跟随一粒沙走完上坡、滑落、被覆盖、再露出的全过程，便能解释沙丘整体前移。
先从全球沙地面积讲起，再指出常见的是延伸成长条波形的线形沙丘。
古老迷信得到科学解释
传说把巨响归于危险精灵，研究者以沙粒同步滑动带动空气振动解释它。
flow: 移动的沙丘会逼近石油设施和铁路，作者由这个实际问题转向沙丘的种类，先介绍常见的线形沙丘。
追踪新月形沙丘怎样移动
锁定风向和供沙条件后，作者跟着一粒沙上坡、滑落，再借沙丘碰撞后恢复形状，解释沙丘如何边走边保持轮廓。
从沙丘的歌声走进实验室
沙粒同步滑动为传说中的轰鸣提供了解释，研究者又在实验室处理沙粒，检验怎样才能让它们发声。

items.en: What are we told about linear dunes?
correct: They develop in a recognisable shape.
它们以可辨识的形状发展

items.en: Bagnold discovered that movement in barchans was caused by
items.zh: 巴格诺德发现在巴沙尔的移动是由
correct: the particular composition of the dunes.

items.en: Why does Dr Douady compare a barchan dune to a living organism?
items.zh: 为什么杜瓦迪博士要把巴氏沙丘和活生物体作比较？
correct: Its outline stays the same even after a period of movement.
即使经过一段时间的移动，其大纲仍然保持不变。

items.en: Singing dunes, which belong to the type of dunes known as ________, produce a very loud sound which is transmitted at a low frequency.
items.zh: 会发声的沙丘属于一种叫作 ________ 的沙丘，它们发出的声音十分响亮，并以低频传播。
items.why: 说明会“唱歌”的沙丘属于barchans。

items.en: Research proves that the individual grains have a similar ________, but the differences in dimensions alter the ____ (Q39) of the ‘song’.
items.zh: 研究表明，每颗沙粒的 ________ 相似，但尺寸差异会改变沙丘“歌声”的 ________（Q39）。

items.en: Research proves that the individual grains have a similar ____ (Q38), but the differences in dimensions alter the ________ of the ‘song’.
items.zh: 研究表明，每颗沙粒的 ________（Q38） 相似，但尺寸差异会改变沙丘“歌声”的 ________。
items.why: 尺寸差异改变“歌曲”的音色/音调。

items.en: Each grain is covered with a mixture of different ________, and this is vital to the sound production.
items.zh: 每颗沙粒都覆盖着由不同 ________ 混合而成的物质，这层覆盖物对发声至关重要。
items.why: 每个颗粒表面覆盖“矿物组合 (desert glaze)”,对发声至关重要。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空最多填两个词。

pairs: 题干的“发现”在原文写作“弄明白”，指巴格诺德解释了沙丘如何一粒沙一粒沙地移动。
题干用“轮廓”指沙丘的外形。原文用 shapes，讨论沙丘相撞后重新形成的独特形状。
dimensions 和 size 都指沙粒的尺寸，alter 和 affect 都把尺寸差异与音调变化联系起来。
points: 先从全球沙地面积讲起，再指出常见的是延伸成长条波形的线形沙丘。
每个颗粒表面覆盖“矿物组合 (desert glaze)”,对发声至关重要。
clauses: However, their insidious creep can have serious consequences ….
连接词 if 引出“if there is an oil installation or a railway line in their path”，说明主句的条件关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 if 把这一层关系补进去。
More grains follow the same pattern, ….
连接词 until 引出“until the accumulated weight of piled-up sand finally pushes the top down the dune face”，说明主句的时间关系。
先读主句的动作，再用 until 把这一层关系补进去。
lead: Things don’t come much stranger than heaps of sand that can move and sing of their own accord.
事情不会变得比一堆沙子更陌生能够随心所欲地移动和歌唱
vocabulary: 逐渐造成危害而不易察觉的
